$comment: Hand-written JSON schemas for what Kestra's export cannot describe: egret's own task types, and the script tasks' taskRunner, whose Kestra definition offers Process (refused by egret) and lacks Kubernetes (Enterprise-only in Kestra, implemented by egret). spec::schema adds the base task properties (id, type, description, retry, timeout, disabled, runIf, allowFailure, allowWarning) to every type here, and `id`/`type` to its `required`. See README.md.

egret.sql.title: Run one SQL statement on a database connection registered in this workspace.
egret.sql.markdownDescription:
egret's own task. `database` is the id of a connection registered in this workspace; publish refuses an id this workspace does not hold. Every `{{ }}` in `sql` is bound as a parameter, never spliced into the text.

The statement runs as the flow's creator, so only the creator can publish or start a flow that contains this task, and a schedule, webhook, Flow trigger or `Subflow` starts it only from a source the creator published.

`fetch` decides the outputs: `NONE` gives `{}`, `FETCH_ONE` gives `size` and `row`, `FETCH` gives `size` and `rows` (at most 10,000 rows; more fails the task), `STORE` writes the rows to internal storage as Ion and gives `size` and `uri`.

database.title: The registered database connection, by id.
database.markdownDescription: The connection's id (a UUID), checked at publish against this workspace. A name is refused.

sql.title: The statement to run.
sql.markdownDescription: A template: every `{{ … }}` in it is bound as a parameter.

fetch.title: What the task does with the rows.
fetch.markdownDescription:
Kestra's JDBC `fetchType` spellings, under egret's own key.

Default value is : `NONE`

x-egret-outputs.name: row
x-egret-outputs.description: The first row, with `fetch: FETCH_ONE` and a statement that returned one.

x-egret-outputs.name: size
x-egret-outputs.description: How many rows the statement returned (`FETCH_ONE`, `FETCH`, `STORE`).

x-egret-outputs.name: uri
x-egret-outputs.description: The internal-storage URI of the Ion file, with `fetch: STORE`.

egret.dataapi.call.title: Call a Data API endpoint of this workspace.
egret.dataapi.call.markdownDescription:
egret's own task. `endpoint` is the id of a Data API endpoint of this workspace; publish refuses an id this workspace does not hold.

**No egret deployment runs this type yet**: publish and every start refuse a flow that uses it (`task_type_not_served`), and the flow schema does not offer it.

endpoint.title: The Data API endpoint, by id.
endpoint.markdownDescription: The endpoint's id (a UUID), checked at publish against this workspace. A name is refused.

egret.report.send.title: Send a chart of this workspace as a report.
egret.report.send.markdownDescription:
egret's own task. `chart` names a chart of this workspace by id; publish cannot yet prove a chart's workspace, so it refuses every `chart`.

**No egret deployment runs this type yet**: publish and every start refuse a flow that uses it (`task_type_not_served`), and the flow schema does not offer it.

egret.taskRunner.title: The task runner to use.
egret.taskRunner.markdownDescription: Absent: the runner this egret is configured with (`workflow.container_runner`). Written: it must be that same runner. `io.kestra.plugin.core.runner.Process` is refused, because it would run the commands inside egret's own server.

delete.title: Whether the container is deleted when it completes.

cpus.title: How many CPUs the container may use, e.g. 1.5.

memory.title: The hard memory limit, e.g. 512m or 2g.

delete.title: Whether the pod is deleted when it completes.

resources.title: The pod's resource requests and limits.
